subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` session route state be owned by the Codex doctor contract, a dedicated OpenAI doctor contract, or generic doctor repair when stale auto overrides no longer match the configured route?
rationale: `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider id and the current Codex app-server route for OpenAI agent turns, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary on its own.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical route state
options.body: Add or expose an OpenAI doctor ownership path for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and regression-test stale auto overrides for non-OpenAI configured agents.

options.title: Codex owns OpenAI app-server route
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor owner if maintainers define Codex as the owner for OpenAI app-server session pins.

options.title: Generic stale auto cleanup
options.body: Make core doctor clear auto-sourced overrides whose provider/model are outside the configured route without relying on provider ownership metadata.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical route state
recommendation.body: Add or expose an OpenAI doctor ownership path for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and regression-test stale auto overrides for non-OpenAI configured agents.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the generic doctor route-state repair and later Codex/OpenAI route repairs, making him the strongest available owner for the boundary decision.
